# Overview {#sec-overview}

## Purpose

This document is the consolidated data-processing pipeline for the
*Drinking Water and Environmental Justice* data brief (`drinking_water.qmd`).
It runs, end to end, every data-acquisition and processing step documented
in that brief's Methodology section:

1. **Service area boundaries** — EPA community water system service area
   polygons for Cook County (@sec-boundaries).
2. **Violation and compliance data** — EPA SDWIS/ECHO Safe Drinking Water
   Act records, summarized by water system and joined to the boundaries
   (@sec-sdwis).
3. **Lead service line inventories** — Illinois EPA's annual Service Line
   Material Inventory reports, standardized and joined to the service
   areas (@sec-lsl).
4. **Unregulated contaminants** — EPA's UCMR 5 monitoring results for 29
   PFAS and lithium, summarized by system and compared with health-based
   reference levels (@sec-ucmr5).

The final steps export every intermediate, detailed, analytical, and
summary dataset to CSV and GeoPackage (@sec-export), then write two
`.RData` files (@sec-save): a lightweight one with only the objects the
*rendered data brief* needs, and a comprehensive one with every dataset.

## Rationale

`drinking_water.qmd` sets `eval: false` globally and shows its Methodology
chunks for documentation purposes only. Those chunks are not meant to be
re-run — and re-download more than 400 MB of EPA data — every time the
brief is rendered. Instead, this pipeline is run separately on a refresh
cadence, and the brief's single evaluated setup chunk (*load prepared
analysis data*) reads this pipeline's GeoPackage
(`data/drinking_water_dataprep.gpkg`) to make `cook_county`,
`cook_cws_with_violations`, and `ucmr5_cook_system_contaminant` available
to the Analysis section, including its interactive leaflet map.

## Usage

Render (or run) this document with the working directory set to its own
folder (`scripts/qmd/`), which matches the relative `data/` paths used
throughout `drinking_water.qmd`. Quarto does this automatically when
rendering:

```bash
quarto render drinking_water_dataprep.qmd
```

To run the code without producing an HTML report, extract it to a plain R
script and source it from an R session started in `scripts/qmd/`:

```r
knitr::purl("drinking_water_dataprep.qmd")
source("drinking_water_dataprep.R")
```

## Outputs

All outputs are written under `scripts/qmd/data/`, and the folders are
created if missing. The pipeline also needs one input that must be
downloaded by hand: IEPA's `ServiceLineMaterialInventoryReports.csv`,
saved to the `data/` folder (see @sec-lsl).

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `data/csv/<dataset>.csv` | One CSV per dataset, across all four tiers (intermediate, detailed, analytical, summary); see @sec-export for the full list |
| `data/csv/dataset_manifest.csv` | One row per exported dataset: tier, description, size, geometry type, file locations |
| `data/csv/data_dictionary.csv` | One row per column of every exported dataset: R class and share missing |
| `data/drinking_water_dataprep.gpkg` | GeoPackage with one layer per dataset (spatial layers and attribute tables), plus the manifest and data dictionary. `drinking_water.qmd` imports its spatial data from this file |
| `data/drinking_water_dataprep.RData` | Essential objects for the brief, as native R objects (the brief imports spatial data from the GeoPackage instead) |
| `data/drinking_water_dataprep_all.RData` | Comprehensive file with every exported dataset, the manifest, the data dictionary, and run information (@sec-save-all) |
| `data/spatial/cook_county_water_system_boundaries.gpkg` | Cook County community water system service areas (standalone copy) |
| `data/spatial/cook_county_water_systems_with_violations.gpkg` | Service areas joined to system-level violation summaries (standalone copy) |

All spatial data are saved as GeoPackage, not Shapefile. Shapefiles cut
field names to 10 characters (so `most_recent_violation_year` and the
`lsl_*` and `ucmr5_*` fields would be renamed) and do not store dates,
times, or logical values reliably. GeoPackage keeps full field names and
types in a single file.

# Setup {#sec-setup}

## Load packages

The following chunk attaches the packages used throughout the pipeline,
with a short note on what each one is used for.

```{r}
#| label: load-packages

library(dplyr)      # data wrangling
library(tidyr)      # replace_na
library(stringr)    # str_starts, str_to_upper
library(readr)      # read_csv, write_csv
library(sf)         # spatial operations
library(httr2)      # ArcGIS REST Feature Service queries (see fetch_arcgis_features())
library(geojsonsf)  # parse ArcGIS REST GeoJSON responses into sf
library(tigris)     # counties()
library(ggplot2)    # quick visual QA plot
library(purrr)      # pmap_dfr, map_dfr for dataset export
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Why not `arcgislayers`?

This pipeline deliberately does **not** use the `arcgislayers` package.
`arcgislayers` requires `rlang >= 1.3.0`, and on systems where
administrative policy pins `rlang` to an older version (e.g. 1.1.7),
calling any `arcgislayers` function (even `arc_open()`) fails with
*"namespace 'rlang' ... is already loaded, but >= 1.3.0 is required"*.
`rlang` cannot be reloaded at a different version mid-session once another
attached package (`dplyr`, `tidyr`, etc.) has already loaded it. All ArcGIS
REST Feature Service access below instead goes through
`fetch_arcgis_features()` (`httr2` + `geojsonsf`; see @sec-arcgis-helpers),
which has no `rlang` version requirement beyond what `dplyr`/`tidyr`
already need.
:::

## Configure spatial engine and output paths

EPA's Public Water System Service Area Boundaries dataset includes some
invalid polygons (self-intersections, duplicate vertices), especially among
EPA-modeled boundaries. `sf`'s default spherical geometry engine (`s2`) is
strict about validity and will error on these, so the next chunk falls back
to the more forgiving GEOS planar engine for the duration of the pipeline.
Geometries are still explicitly repaired with `st_make_valid()` as a second
safeguard. The chunk also defines the output locations and creates the
output folders if they do not already exist. Downloaded source files go
to `data/tabular/`; the datasets the pipeline produces are exported to
`data/csv/` and `data/drinking_water_dataprep.gpkg` in @sec-export.

```{r}
#| label: configure-environment

sf::sf_use_s2(FALSE)

out_spatial_dir    <- "data/spatial"
out_tabular_dir    <- "data/tabular"   # downloaded and extracted source files
out_csv_dir        <- "data/csv"       # exported datasets, one CSV each (@sec-export)
out_gpkg_path      <- "data/drinking_water_dataprep.gpkg"
out_rdata_path     <- "data/drinking_water_dataprep.RData"
out_rdata_all_path <- "data/drinking_water_dataprep_all.RData"

dir.create(out_spatial_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(out_tabular_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(out_csv_dir,     showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
```

# Public Water System Service Area Boundaries {#sec-boundaries}

This section mirrors the brief's Methodology subsection *Public Water
System Service Area Boundaries*. It retrieves community water system
service area polygons from EPA's hosted ArcGIS Feature Service and clips
them to Cook County.

**Source:** EPA Office of Water, [Public Water System Service Area
Boundaries v3](https://www.epa.gov/ground-water-and-drinking-water/public-water-system-service-areas).

The chunk below stores the Feature Service URL used throughout this
section.

```{r}
#| label: boundaries-feature-server-url

feature_server_url <- "https://services.arcgis.com/cJ9YHowT8TU7DUyn/arcgis/rest/services/Water_System_Boundaries/FeatureServer"
```

## Cook County boundary

The national boundaries dataset contains more than 44,000 systems. To avoid
downloading all of them, the Cook County polygon is retrieved from the
Census Bureau's cartographic boundary files (via `tigris`) and used as a
spatial filter. It is projected to WGS 84 (EPSG:4326) to match the Feature
Service.

```{r}
#| label: cook-county-boundary

cook_county <- counties(state = "IL", cb = TRUE, year = 2023) %>%
  filter(NAME == "Cook") %>%
  st_transform(4326)
```

## ArcGIS REST Feature Service helpers {#sec-arcgis-helpers}

These two helper functions cover everything `arcgislayers` would otherwise
provide for this pipeline: inspecting a FeatureServer's layer list, and
paginated feature retrieval with an optional bounding-box spatial filter.

### Listing available layers

`print_arcgis_layers()` is a lightweight replacement for `arc_open()` +
`print()`. It fetches and prints the FeatureServer's layer listing so the
correct layer index can be confirmed (a service may expose more than one
layer, e.g. active vs. historical).

```{r}
#| label: fn-print-arcgis-layers

print_arcgis_layers <- function(base_url) {
  service_info <- request(base_url) %>%
    req_url_query(f = "json") %>%
    req_perform() %>%
    resp_body_json()

  layers <- service_info$layers
  if (length(layers) == 0) {
    message("No layers reported for ", base_url)
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }

  message("Layers available on ", base_url, ":")
  for (lyr in layers) {
    message(sprintf("  [%s] %s", lyr$id, lyr$name))
  }
  invisible(service_info)
}
```

### Paginated feature retrieval

`fetch_arcgis_features()` replaces `arc_select()`. It queries an ArcGIS
REST Feature Service layer and returns the result as an `sf` object. Esri
REST services usually cap each response at roughly 1,000–2,000 records
(`maxRecordCount`), so the function pages through results with
`resultOffset` until a short or empty page signals the last one. When
`geometry_sf` is supplied, its bounding box is sent as a cheap server-side
prefilter (mirroring `arc_select(filter_geom = ...)`); callers refine the
result afterward with an exact `st_filter()`.

```{r}
#| label: fn-fetch-arcgis-features

fetch_arcgis_features <- function(base_url, layer_id = 0, where = "1=1",
                                   out_fields = "*", geometry_sf = NULL,
                                   batch_size = 1000) {
  query_url <- paste0(base_url, "/", layer_id, "/query")

  # Bounding-box prefilter (server-side), refined with st_filter() afterward.
  geom_param <- NULL
  if (!is.null(geometry_sf)) {
    bb <- st_bbox(st_transform(geometry_sf, 4326))
    geom_param <- sprintf(
      '{"xmin":%f,"ymin":%f,"xmax":%f,"ymax":%f,"spatialReference":{"wkid":4326}}',
      bb["xmin"], bb["ymin"], bb["xmax"], bb["ymax"]
    )
  }

  all_features <- list()
  offset <- 0
  repeat {
    req <- request(query_url) %>%
      req_url_query(
        where = where,
        outFields = out_fields,
        f = "geojson",
        resultOffset = offset,
        resultRecordCount = batch_size,
        geometry = geom_param,
        geometryType = if (!is.null(geom_param)) "esriGeometryEnvelope" else NULL,
        inSR = if (!is.null(geom_param)) 4326 else NULL,
        spatialRel = if (!is.null(geom_param)) "esriSpatialRelIntersects" else NULL
      )

    resp <- req_perform(req)
    txt <- resp_body_string(resp)

    batch_sf <- geojson_sf(txt)
    if (nrow(batch_sf) == 0) break

    all_features[[length(all_features) + 1]] <- batch_sf
    if (nrow(batch_sf) < batch_size) break
    offset <- offset + batch_size
  }

  if (length(all_features) == 0) {
    return(all_features)  # empty list -- caller decides how to handle
  }

  dplyr::bind_rows(all_features) %>%
    st_as_sf() %>%
    st_make_valid()
}
```

## Retrieve Cook County community water system boundaries

First, the FeatureServer's layers are listed to confirm that layer `0` is
the main community water system boundaries layer.

```{r}
#| label: list-boundary-layers

print_arcgis_layers(feature_server_url)
```

Next, only features whose bounding box intersects the Cook County boundary
are pulled from layer `0`. The pipeline stops with an informative error if
nothing is returned, since every later step depends on these boundaries.

```{r}
#| label: fetch-boundaries

cook_cws_raw <- fetch_arcgis_features(
  base_url    = feature_server_url,
  layer_id    = 0,
  geometry_sf = cook_county
)

if (length(cook_cws_raw) == 0 || nrow(cook_cws_raw) == 0) {
  stop("No community water system boundary features were returned for the ",
       "Cook County bounding box -- check feature_server_url and the ",
       "FeatureServer's availability before continuing.")
}
```

Finally, invalid geometries are repaired, any features that remain invalid
are dropped (with a message reporting how many), and the result is clipped
precisely to the Cook County polygon.

```{r}
#| label: clean-clip-boundaries

cook_cws_valid <- cook_cws_raw %>%
  st_make_valid()

n_invalid <- sum(!st_is_valid(cook_cws_valid))
if (n_invalid > 0) {
  message(n_invalid, " feature(s) remain invalid after st_make_valid(); ",
          "these will be dropped before clipping.")
  cook_cws_valid <- cook_cws_valid[st_is_valid(cook_cws_valid), ]
}

cook_cws <- cook_cws_valid %>%
  st_filter(cook_county, .predicate = st_intersects)  # precise clip to county polygon
```

## Save and quality check

The next chunk prints a compact summary of the boundary attributes and
writes the boundaries to a GeoPackage.

```{r}
#| label: save-boundaries

glimpse(st_drop_geometry(cook_cws))

st_write(cook_cws, file.path(out_spatial_dir, "cook_county_water_system_boundaries.gpkg"),
         delete_dsn = TRUE, quiet = TRUE)
```

As a quick visual check, the service areas are mapped within the Cook
County outline, with each system shaded a different color.

```{r}
#| label: fig-boundaries-qa
#| fig-cap: "Community water system service areas, Cook County, IL"

print(
  ggplot() +
    geom_sf(data = cook_county, fill = NA, color = "black", linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_sf(data = cook_cws, aes(fill = PWS_Name), color = "white", linewidth = 0.1,
            show.legend = FALSE, alpha = 0.85) +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(
      title = "Community Water System Service Areas, Cook County, IL",
      caption = "Source: U.S. EPA Public Water System Service Area Boundaries (v3)"
    )
)
```

## Notes

- This layer covers **community** water systems only. Non-community systems
  (schools, gas stations, small transient supplies) are published in a
  separate FeatureServer.
- The boundary data mixes EPA-modeled boundaries with authoritative
  state/utility-sourced boundaries. Check the `SOURCE`/`DATA_SRC` field to
  distinguish modeled estimates from verified boundaries.

# Drinking Water Violation and Compliance (SDWIS/ECHO) {#sec-sdwis}

This section mirrors the brief's Methodology subsection *Drinking Water
Violation and Compliance*. It downloads EPA's bulk Safe Drinking Water Act
(SDWA) dataset, narrows it to Cook County water systems, decodes key
fields, summarizes violations by system, and joins that summary to the
service area boundaries from @sec-boundaries.

**Sources:** EPA ECHO – SDWA Data Downloads
([summary and data dictionary](https://echo.epa.gov/tools/data-downloads/sdwa-download-summary);
[bulk download index](https://echo.epa.gov/files/echodownloads/)).

The chunk below defines the download URL and the local path for the ZIP
archive.

```{r}
#| label: sdwa-paths

zip_url  <- "https://echo.epa.gov/files/echodownloads/SDWA_latest_downloads.zip"
zip_path <- file.path(out_tabular_dir, "SDWA_latest_downloads.zip")
```

## Download the bulk SDWA dataset

The bulk dataset is a single large ZIP of CSVs (400+ MB) covering every
public water system nationally, refreshed by EPA quarterly. It is only
downloaded if a local copy is not already present; delete the ZIP to force
a refresh.

```{r}
#| label: download-sdwa

if (!file.exists(zip_path)) {
  download.file(zip_url, destfile = zip_path, mode = "wb")
}
```

## Extract required files

Only the six tables used by this pipeline are extracted. File names are
matched case-insensitively in case EPA changes casing between quarterly
releases, and any expected files that are missing are reported along with
the archive's full contents to help diagnose naming changes.

```{r}
#| label: extract-sdwa

needed_files <- c(
  "SDWA_PUB_WATER_SYSTEMS.csv",
  "SDWA_VIOLATIONS_ENFORCEMENT.csv",
  "SDWA_GEOGRAPHIC_AREAS.csv",
  "SDWA_SERVICE_AREAS.csv",
  "SDWA_REF_CODE_VALUES.csv",
  "SDWA_LCR_SAMPLES.csv"          # Lead & Copper Rule sample data
)

zip_contents <- unzip(zip_path, list = TRUE)$Name

files_to_extract <- zip_contents[
  toupper(zip_contents) %in% toupper(needed_files)
]

missing <- setdiff(toupper(needed_files), toupper(files_to_extract))
if (length(missing) > 0) {
  message("Note: the following expected files were not found in this quarter's ZIP: ",
          paste(missing, collapse = ", "),
          "\nCheck zip_contents (printed below) for the current file list/naming.")
  print(zip_contents)
}

unzip(zip_path, files = files_to_extract, exdir = out_tabular_dir, overwrite = TRUE)
```

## Read and filter to Illinois

The first two characters of each `PWSID` are the state/region code (e.g.
`IL`), so every table can be filtered to Illinois systems on read, before
any joins. The helper `read_il()` does this and returns `NULL` if a file is
absent. The reference-code table is not state-specific and is small, so it
is read in full.

```{r}
#| label: read-sdwa

read_il <- function(filename) {
  path <- file.path(out_tabular_dir, filename)
  if (!file.exists(path)) return(NULL)
  read_csv(path, guess_max = 100000, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    filter(str_starts(PWSID, "IL"))
}

pws         <- read_il("SDWA_PUB_WATER_SYSTEMS.csv")
violations  <- read_il("SDWA_VIOLATIONS_ENFORCEMENT.csv")
geo_areas   <- read_il("SDWA_GEOGRAPHIC_AREAS.csv")
svc_areas   <- read_il("SDWA_SERVICE_AREAS.csv")
lcr_samples <- read_il("SDWA_LCR_SAMPLES.csv")

ref_codes <- read_csv(file.path(out_tabular_dir, "SDWA_REF_CODE_VALUES.csv"),
                       show_col_types = FALSE)
```

## Narrow to Cook County systems

The `COUNTY_SERVED` field in `SDWA_GEOGRAPHIC_AREAS.csv` is the most direct
way to identify Cook County systems within the Illinois subset. Because it
is self-reported by water systems and states, it may be incomplete;
discrepancies against the boundary-based approach in @sec-boundaries are
retained and reported rather than reconciled. The chunk below builds the
list of Cook County `PWSID`s and filters the system, violation, and Lead
and Copper Rule sample tables to it.

```{r}
#| label: filter-cook-county

cook_pwsids <- geo_areas %>%
  filter(str_to_upper(COUNTY_SERVED) == "COOK") %>%
  distinct(PWSID) %>%
  pull(PWSID)

message(length(cook_pwsids), " unique PWSIDs identified as serving Cook County ",
        "via the COUNTY_SERVED field.")

pws_cook        <- pws        %>% filter(PWSID %in% cook_pwsids)
violations_cook <- violations %>% filter(PWSID %in% cook_pwsids)
lcr_cook        <- lcr_samples %>% filter(PWSID %in% cook_pwsids)
```

## Decode coded fields

Violation and contaminant codes are stored as numeric/alphanumeric codes.
The helper `decode()` looks up a given `VALUE_TYPE` in the reference-code
table and joins its human-readable description onto the data as a new
column. It is applied here to add violation and contaminant descriptions.

```{r}
#| label: decode-fields

decode <- function(df, code_col, value_type, new_col) {
  lookup <- ref_codes %>%
    filter(VALUE_TYPE == value_type) %>%
    select(VALUE_CODE, VALUE_DESCRIPTION) %>%
    rename(!!new_col := VALUE_DESCRIPTION)

  df %>%
    left_join(lookup, by = setNames("VALUE_CODE", code_col))
}

violations_cook <- violations_cook %>%
  decode("VIOLATION_CODE", "VIOLATION_CODE", "violation_description") %>%
  decode("CONTAMINANT_CODE", "CONTAMINANT_CODE", "contaminant_description")
```

## Summarize violations by system

The next chunk counts, for each water system, total violations,
health-based violations, unresolved violations, and Lead and Copper Rule
violations, along with the most recent violation date. These counts are
then joined onto a subset of system attributes, with zero filled in for
systems that have no recorded violations.

Key field definitions:

- **`OWNER_TYPE_CODE`**: F = Federal, L = Local government, M =
  Public/Private, N = Native American, P = Private, S = State.
- **`RULE_CODE == "350"`** isolates Lead and Copper Rule violations.
- **`VIOLATION_STATUS`** values *Unaddressed* and *Addressed* (as opposed
  to *Resolved*/*Archived*) are treated as **unresolved**, i.e. not yet
  subject to a resolving enforcement action, per EPA's compliance status
  categories.

### Parse violation dates

`VIOL_LAST_REPORTED_DATE` is read in as a character field (EPA ECHO
exports dates as `MM/DD/YYYY`). Taking the maximum of these strings would
compare them alphabetically rather than chronologically (e.g.
`"12/01/2015"` sorts after `"01/15/2023"`), so the helper below converts
them to `Date` values *before* the most recent violation is identified.
It accepts both `MM/DD/YYYY` and ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` formats, ignores any
trailing time component, and passes through values `read_csv()` has
already parsed as dates.

```{r}
#| label: fn-parse-violation-date

parse_violation_date <- function(x) {
  if (inherits(x, "Date")) return(x)
  if (inherits(x, "POSIXt")) return(as.Date(x))
  x <- trimws(as.character(x))
  coalesce(
    as.Date(x, format = "%m/%d/%Y"),
    as.Date(x, format = "%Y-%m-%d")
  )
}
```

### Summarize by system

The chunk below computes the system-level counts and the most recent
violation date (a `Date`, or `NA` if a system has no dated violations),
then adds `most_recent_violation_year`, a numeric year derived from that
date, for filtering and mapping by year.

```{r}
#| label: summarize-violations

violation_summary <- violations_cook %>%
  mutate(viol_last_reported_date = parse_violation_date(VIOL_LAST_REPORTED_DATE)) %>%
  group_by(PWSID) %>%
  summarise(
    n_violations           = n(),
    n_health_based         = sum(IS_HEALTH_BASED_IND == "Y", na.rm = TRUE),
    n_unresolved           = sum(VIOLATION_STATUS %in% c("Unaddressed", "Addressed"), na.rm = TRUE),
    n_lead_copper_rule     = sum(RULE_CODE == "350", na.rm = TRUE),
    most_recent_violation  = if (all(is.na(viol_last_reported_date))) as.Date(NA)
                             else max(viol_last_reported_date, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(most_recent_violation_year = as.numeric(format(most_recent_violation, "%Y")))

pws_cook_summary <- pws_cook %>%
  select(PWSID, PWS_NAME, OWNER_TYPE_CODE, POPULATION_SERVED_COUNT,
         PRIMARY_SOURCE_CODE, PWS_ACTIVITY_CODE, SERVICE_CONNECTIONS_COUNT) %>%
  left_join(violation_summary, by = "PWSID") %>%
  mutate(across(starts_with("n_"), ~ replace_na(.x, 0)))
```

## Join violations to service area boundaries

This is the key spatial–tabular join. It attaches the system-level
violation summary to the service area polygons by `PWSID`, producing
`cook_cws_with_violations` — the `sf` object on which the brief's
interactive leaflet map is built. It carries `most_recent_violation` as a
`Date` and `most_recent_violation_year` as a number.

Both tables have a system name field: `PWS_Name` from the boundaries and
`PWS_NAME` from SDWIS. GeoPackage (like SQLite) treats column names that
differ only in case as the same column, so the SDWIS name is renamed to
`PWS_NAME_SDWIS` in the join. The result is saved as a GeoPackage, which
keeps the full field names. The version with every joined field (lead
service lines and UCMR 5) is exported in @sec-export.

```{r}
#| label: join-violations-boundaries

cook_cws_with_violations <- cook_cws %>%
  left_join(rename(pws_cook_summary, PWS_NAME_SDWIS = PWS_NAME), by = "PWSID")

st_write(cook_cws_with_violations,
         file.path(out_spatial_dir, "cook_county_water_systems_with_violations.gpkg"),
         delete_dsn = TRUE, quiet = TRUE)
```

## Notes

- Filtering on the `PWSID` prefix (`str_starts(PWSID, "IL")`) captures
  Illinois-primacy systems. A small number of tribal systems may be coded
  under an EPA region prefix instead; check `EPA_REGION` if tribal systems
  are in scope.
- This is quarterly-snapshot data (`SUBMISSIONYEARQUARTER` field). A
  violations *history* over time would require EPA's cumulative-year bulk
  download or the individual violations file's date fields.

# Lead Service Lines {#sec-lsl}

This section mirrors the brief's Methodology subsection *Lead Service
Lines*. It uses the Illinois Environmental Protection Agency's (IEPA)
statewide **Service Line Material Inventory Reports**, which community
water supplies submit to IEPA each year under the Lead Service Line
Replacement and Notification Act (415 ILCS 5/17.12). Each report gives a
system-level count of service lines by material (lead, galvanized, copper,
plastic, unknown, etc.), keyed to the system's `PWSID`. Because these
reports cover every community water supply in a consistent format, they
replace the earlier approach of locating and aggregating individual
municipal ArcGIS lead service line maps.

**Source:** Illinois EPA, [Lead Service Line
Information](https://epa.illinois.gov/topics/drinking-water/public-water-users/lead-service-line-information.html)
(file `ServiceLineMaterialInventoryReports.csv`).

## Locate the inventory file

The CSV is downloaded manually from the IEPA page above and saved to the
project's `data/` folder; it is not retrieved automatically. The chunk
below looks for it in `data/` relative to this document (`scripts/qmd/data/`),
in `data/tabular/`, and in the repository-level `data/` folder. The name
is matched loosely, so a browser-renamed copy (for example,
`ServiceLineMaterialInventoryReports (1).csv`) is still found. If the file
is in none of these places, the chunk stops and prints the full folder
paths searched and the current working directory.

```{r}
#| label: lsl-inventory-path

lsl_search_dirs <- c("data", out_tabular_dir, file.path("..", "..", "data"))

## Match the file name loosely, so a browser-renamed download such as
## "ServiceLineMaterialInventoryReports (1).csv" is still found.
lsl_inventory_candidates <- unlist(lapply(lsl_search_dirs, function(d) {
  if (!dir.exists(d)) return(character(0))
  list.files(d, pattern = "(?i)^ServiceLineMaterialInventoryReports.*\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)
}))

lsl_inventory_path <- lsl_inventory_candidates[1]

if (is.na(lsl_inventory_path)) {
  stop("ServiceLineMaterialInventoryReports.csv was not found.\n",
       "  1. Download it from ",
       "https://epa.illinois.gov/topics/drinking-water/public-water-users/lead-service-line-information.html\n",
       "  2. Save it to one of these folders:\n    ",
       paste(normalizePath(lsl_search_dirs, mustWork = FALSE), collapse = "\n    "), "\n",
       "  Current working directory: ", getwd(),
       " (run this pipeline from scripts/qmd/).")
}

message("Reading IEPA service line inventory from ", lsl_inventory_path)
```

## Read and filter to Cook County systems

The file contains one row per water system per reporting year
(2017–2024) for every community water supply in Illinois. It is read with
explicit column types (all count fields as integers), and the
`ReportedDate` timestamp is parsed to a date-time.

Systems are retained if IEPA lists their county as Cook **or** their
`PWSID` (`FacilityId`) appears among the Cook County systems identified
in @sec-sdwis or the service area boundaries retrieved in
@sec-boundaries. The second condition keeps systems that serve Cook
County residents but are listed under a neighboring county, so that every
mapped service area can be matched to an inventory where one exists.

```{r}
#| label: read-lsl-inventory

lsl_count_cols <- c(
  "TotalServiceConnections", "WholesaleConnections", "RetailConnections",
  "ServicesLead", "ServicesUnknownMaterial", "ServicesCopperLeadSolder",
  "ServicesGalvanized", "ServicesUnknownNotLead", "ServicesCopperNonLeadSolder",
  "ServicesCastDuctileIronTransite", "ServicesPlastic"
)

lsl_raw <- read_csv(
  lsl_inventory_path,
  col_types = cols(
    .default      = col_integer(),
    FacilityId    = col_character(),
    County        = col_character(),
    FacilityName  = col_character(),
    ReportedDate  = col_character(),
    ReportingYear = col_integer()
  )
) %>%
  mutate(ReportedDate = as.POSIXct(ReportedDate, format = "%m/%d/%Y %I:%M:%S %p",
                                   tz = "America/Chicago"))

cook_lsl_pwsids <- union(cook_pwsids, cook_cws$PWSID)

lsl_cook_raw <- lsl_raw %>%
  filter(County == "Cook" | FacilityId %in% cook_lsl_pwsids) %>%
  mutate(county_listed_cook = County == "Cook")

message(n_distinct(lsl_cook_raw$FacilityId), " water systems and ",
        nrow(lsl_cook_raw), " system-year inventory reports retained for Cook County.")
```

## Standardize service line material categories

The eight material columns are collapsed into four material categories
that match the regulatory distinctions used in lead service line
replacement, plus an *unclassified* count described below:

- **Lead** (`ServicesLead`).
- **Galvanized** (`ServicesGalvanized`). Under federal and Illinois rules,
  galvanized lines that are or were downstream of lead must also be
  replaced.
- **Unknown material** (`ServicesUnknownMaterial`). These lines may be lead
  and are treated as such for replacement planning until verified.
- **Non-lead** (copper with or without lead solder, cast/ductile iron or
  transite, plastic, and "unknown but not lead").

The reporting form changed over time. Reports for 2024 include only lead
and unknown counts, with every other material column left at zero, and
some 2022 reports do not fully break down the total. Any service lines
not assigned to a material category are therefore kept in a separate
**unclassified** count (total connections minus all reported categories)
rather than assumed to be non-lead. Shares are calculated against total
service connections, and `lsl_pct_lead_or_unknown` combines lead,
galvanized, and unknown lines as the share of lines that may require
replacement.

```{r}
#| label: standardize-lsl-categories

cook_lsl_history <- lsl_cook_raw %>%
  mutate(
    lsl_total       = TotalServiceConnections,
    lsl_lead        = ServicesLead,
    lsl_galvanized  = ServicesGalvanized,
    lsl_unknown     = ServicesUnknownMaterial,
    lsl_non_lead    = ServicesCopperLeadSolder + ServicesCopperNonLeadSolder +
                      ServicesCastDuctileIronTransite + ServicesPlastic +
                      ServicesUnknownNotLead,
    lsl_unclassified = pmax(lsl_total - (lsl_lead + lsl_galvanized + lsl_unknown + lsl_non_lead), 0L),
    lsl_pct_lead            = if_else(lsl_total > 0, lsl_lead / lsl_total, NA_real_),
    lsl_pct_unknown         = if_else(lsl_total > 0, lsl_unknown / lsl_total, NA_real_),
    lsl_pct_lead_or_unknown = if_else(lsl_total > 0,
                                      (lsl_lead + lsl_galvanized + lsl_unknown) / lsl_total,
                                      NA_real_)
  ) %>%
  arrange(FacilityId, ReportingYear)
```

## Identify each system's most recent inventory

Not every system reports every year. Only about a third of Cook County
systems appear in the 2024 reports, and most systems' latest report is
from 2022. The chunk below keeps each system's most recent report
(latest `ReportingYear`, then latest `ReportedDate` if a year is
duplicated) and records which year it comes from in `lsl_reporting_year`,
so comparisons across systems can account for differences in reporting
year.

```{r}
#| label: latest-lsl-inventory

cook_lsl_latest <- cook_lsl_history %>%
  group_by(FacilityId) %>%
  arrange(desc(ReportingYear), desc(ReportedDate), .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  rename(lsl_reporting_year = ReportingYear)

print(count(cook_lsl_latest, lsl_reporting_year, name = "n_systems"))
```

## Summarize inventories by reporting year

As a quick check, the next chunk totals each material category across
Cook County systems for each reporting year. Year-to-year changes reflect
both actual replacements and reclassification of unknown lines, as well
as changes in which systems reported and in the reporting form, so these
totals are descriptive rather than a measure of replacement progress.

```{r}
#| label: lsl-summary-by-year

lsl_summary_by_year <- cook_lsl_history %>%
  group_by(ReportingYear) %>%
  summarise(
    n_systems        = n_distinct(FacilityId),
    lsl_total        = sum(lsl_total, na.rm = TRUE),
    lsl_lead         = sum(lsl_lead, na.rm = TRUE),
    lsl_galvanized   = sum(lsl_galvanized, na.rm = TRUE),
    lsl_unknown      = sum(lsl_unknown, na.rm = TRUE),
    lsl_non_lead     = sum(lsl_non_lead, na.rm = TRUE),
    lsl_unclassified = sum(lsl_unclassified, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(lsl_summary_by_year)
```

## Join inventories to service areas

Each system's most recent inventory is joined by `PWSID` to
`cook_cws_with_violations`, adding the `lsl_*` fields alongside the
violation summary so that lead service line prevalence can be mapped and
compared with compliance history. Service areas with no matching IEPA
report (for example, the Indiana systems) receive `NA` for these fields.
The full history, the latest-report table, and the yearly summary are
exported with the other datasets in @sec-export.

```{r}
#| label: join-lsl

lsl_join_fields <- cook_lsl_latest %>%
  select(PWSID = FacilityId, lsl_reporting_year, lsl_total, lsl_lead,
         lsl_galvanized, lsl_unknown, lsl_non_lead, lsl_unclassified,
         lsl_pct_lead, lsl_pct_unknown, lsl_pct_lead_or_unknown)

cook_cws_with_violations <- cook_cws_with_violations %>%
  left_join(lsl_join_fields, by = "PWSID")

message(sum(!is.na(cook_cws_with_violations$lsl_reporting_year)), " of ",
        nrow(cook_cws_with_violations), " service areas matched to an IEPA inventory report.")
```

## Notes

- Inventories are system-level counts, not line-level or parcel-level
  locations, so they show how many lead lines a system has but not where
  they are within its service area.
- Counts are self-reported by water systems. Large "unknown" counts,
  especially in the 2024 reports, reflect incomplete field verification
  rather than confirmed absence or presence of lead.
- Because the reporting form changed (notably in 2024), compare material
  categories across years with caution and always note the
  `lsl_reporting_year` a figure comes from.
- Wholesale systems report wholesale connections separately
  (`WholesaleConnections`); totals here use `TotalServiceConnections` as
  reported.

# Unregulated Contaminants (UCMR 5) {#sec-ucmr5}

This section mirrors the brief's Methodology subsection *Unregulated
Contaminant Monitoring (UCMR 5)*. The fifth Unregulated Contaminant
Monitoring Rule (UCMR 5) requires public water systems to sample for 30
contaminants that are not yet fully regulated: 29 per- and polyfluoroalkyl
substances (PFAS) and lithium. Monitoring ran from 2023 to 2025 and
covered all community water systems serving more than 3,300 people plus a
representative sample of smaller systems. EPA releases the results in
batches as they are reported, so this section downloads the most recent
release each time it is run.

**Source:** U.S. EPA, [Occurrence Data from the Unregulated Contaminant
Monitoring Rule](https://www.epa.gov/dwucmr/occurrence-data-unregulated-contaminant-monitoring-rule#5).

::: {.callout-important}
## Verify against the current EPA release

The code below follows the published layout of the UCMR 5 occurrence
data file (`UCMR5_All.txt`, tab-delimited). It was written without
access to the live file, so the first run should be checked: the chunk
that reads the file stops with a list of any expected columns that are
missing, and the contaminant names used for reference-level comparisons
should be confirmed against the printed list of contaminants.
:::

## Locate and download the latest release

EPA publishes each UCMR 5 data release as a ZIP file linked from the
occurrence data page, and the file's URL changes with each release. The
helper below reads the page and returns the first linked ZIP whose name
refers to UCMR 5, preferring the occurrence data file. If the page cannot
be read, it falls back to the last known URL.

A ZIP saved by hand to `data/` (or the repository-level `data/` folder)
with "ucmr5" in its name is used instead of downloading, which supports
restricted networks. Set `ucmr5_refresh <- TRUE` to force a fresh download
of the latest release.

```{r}
#| label: ucmr5-locate

ucmr5_page_url        <- "https://www.epa.gov/dwucmr/occurrence-data-unregulated-contaminant-monitoring-rule"
ucmr5_fallback_zip    <- "https://www.epa.gov/system/files/other-files/2023-08/ucmr5-occurrence-data.zip"
ucmr5_zip_path        <- file.path(out_tabular_dir, "ucmr5-occurrence-data.zip")
ucmr5_refresh         <- FALSE

find_ucmr5_zip_url <- function(page_url, fallback) {
  html <- tryCatch(
    request(page_url) %>% req_perform() %>% resp_body_string(),
    error = function(e) {
      message("Could not read the UCMR page (", conditionMessage(e), "); using fallback URL.")
      NULL
    }
  )
  if (is.null(html)) return(fallback)

  hrefs <- str_match_all(html, 'href="([^"]+\\.zip)"')[[1]][, 2]
  hrefs <- hrefs[str_detect(hrefs, regex("ucmr[-_ ]?5", ignore_case = TRUE))]
  if (length(hrefs) == 0) {
    message("No UCMR 5 ZIP link found on the page; using fallback URL.")
    return(fallback)
  }
  hrefs <- hrefs[order(!str_detect(hrefs, regex("occurrence", ignore_case = TRUE)))]
  url <- hrefs[1]
  if (!str_starts(url, "http")) url <- paste0("https://www.epa.gov", url)
  url
}

manual_zips <- c(
  list.files("data", pattern = "(?i)ucmr[-_ ]?5.*\\.zip$", full.names = TRUE),
  list.files(file.path("..", "..", "data"), pattern = "(?i)ucmr[-_ ]?5.*\\.zip$", full.names = TRUE)
)

if (length(manual_zips) > 0 && !ucmr5_refresh) {
  ucmr5_zip_path <- manual_zips[1]
  message("Using manually saved UCMR 5 file: ", ucmr5_zip_path)
} else if (!file.exists(ucmr5_zip_path) || ucmr5_refresh) {
  ucmr5_zip_url <- find_ucmr5_zip_url(ucmr5_page_url, ucmr5_fallback_zip)
  message("Downloading UCMR 5 data from ", ucmr5_zip_url)
  download.file(ucmr5_zip_url, destfile = ucmr5_zip_path, mode = "wb")
}
```

## Extract and read the results file

The ZIP contains the main results file (`UCMR5_All.txt`) along with
supporting files (for example, ZIP codes served and additional data
elements). The chunk below extracts the results file, matching its name
case-insensitively, and reads it as tab-delimited text with every column
as character, so that no values are lost to type guessing. Latin-1
encoding is used because the units field contains the "µ" symbol. The
chunk then checks that the columns used later are present.

```{r}
#| label: ucmr5-read

ucmr5_contents <- unzip(ucmr5_zip_path, list = TRUE)$Name
ucmr5_all_file <- ucmr5_contents[str_detect(ucmr5_contents, regex("UCMR5_All.*\\.txt$", ignore_case = TRUE))][1]

if (is.na(ucmr5_all_file)) {
  print(ucmr5_contents)
  stop("No UCMR5_All results file found in ", ucmr5_zip_path, " (contents printed above).")
}

unzip(ucmr5_zip_path, files = ucmr5_all_file, exdir = out_tabular_dir, overwrite = TRUE)

ucmr5_raw <- read_tsv(
  file.path(out_tabular_dir, ucmr5_all_file),
  col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
  locale = locale(encoding = "latin1"),
  progress = FALSE
)

ucmr5_required_cols <- c("PWSID", "PWSName", "Size", "FacilityID", "SamplePointID",
                         "CollectionDate", "Contaminant", "MRL", "Units",
                         "AnalyticalResultsSign", "AnalyticalResultValue")
ucmr5_missing_cols <- setdiff(ucmr5_required_cols, names(ucmr5_raw))
if (length(ucmr5_missing_cols) > 0) {
  stop("UCMR 5 file is missing expected columns: ", paste(ucmr5_missing_cols, collapse = ", "),
       ". Columns present: ", paste(names(ucmr5_raw), collapse = ", "))
}

message(nrow(ucmr5_raw), " UCMR 5 results read for ", n_distinct(ucmr5_raw$PWSID), " systems nationally.")
```

## Filter to Cook County systems and standardize results

Results are kept for systems identified as serving Cook County in
@sec-sdwis or whose service areas intersect the county (@sec-boundaries),
the same rule used for the lead service line inventories.

Each result is then standardized:

- **Concentrations** are converted to nanograms per liter (ng/L), the unit
  used for PFAS drinking water standards. Results reported in µg/L are
  multiplied by 1,000.
- **Detections** are results with an `AnalyticalResultsSign` of "=",
  meaning the contaminant was measured at or above EPA's minimum reporting
  level (MRL). Results marked "<" were below the MRL and are treated as
  non-detects with a concentration of zero when averaging.
- **Contaminant group** is "Lithium" or "PFAS". Every other UCMR 5
  contaminant is a PFAS.
- **Collection dates** are parsed from either `MM/DD/YYYY` or ISO format.

```{r}
#| label: ucmr5-standardize

ucmr5_cook <- ucmr5_raw %>%
  filter(PWSID %in% union(cook_pwsids, cook_cws$PWSID)) %>%
  mutate(
    result_value    = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(AnalyticalResultValue)),
    mrl_value       = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(MRL)),
    to_ngL          = if_else(str_detect(Units, regex("ng", ignore_case = TRUE)), 1, 1000),
    result_ngL      = result_value * to_ngL,
    mrl_ngL         = mrl_value * to_ngL,
    detected        = AnalyticalResultsSign == "=" & !is.na(result_ngL),
    result_ngL_nd0  = if_else(detected, result_ngL, 0),
    contaminant_key = str_to_upper(str_replace_all(Contaminant, "[^A-Za-z0-9]", "")),
    contaminant_group = if_else(contaminant_key == "LITHIUM", "Lithium", "PFAS"),
    collection_date = coalesce(as.Date(CollectionDate, format = "%m/%d/%Y"),
                               as.Date(CollectionDate, format = "%Y-%m-%d"))
  )

message(n_distinct(ucmr5_cook$PWSID), " Cook County systems have UCMR 5 results (",
        nrow(ucmr5_cook), " results).")

## Confirm the contaminant names match those used in the reference table below.
print(sort(unique(ucmr5_cook$Contaminant)))
```

## Health-based reference levels

UCMR 5 contaminants are unregulated at the time of monitoring, so results
are compared with health-based reference levels rather than enforceable
standards. Two kinds of comparison are made:

- **PFAS:** EPA's 2024 National Primary Drinking Water Regulation set
  maximum contaminant levels (MCLs) of 4.0 ng/L for PFOA and PFOS and
  10 ng/L for PFHxS, PFNA, and HFPO-DA (GenX). It also set a Hazard Index
  of 1 for mixtures of PFHxS, PFNA, HFPO-DA, and PFBS. Each of these four
  is divided by its health-based water concentration (10, 10, 10, and
  2,000 ng/L, respectively) and the ratios are summed. EPA has since
  announced that it intends to keep the PFOA and PFOS limits, extend the
  compliance deadline, and reconsider the others. All five are retained
  here as screening values.
- **Lithium:** EPA's health reference level (HRL) of 10 µg/L (10,000 ng/L),
  used in UCMR 5 reporting.

MCL compliance is based on a running annual average, not on single
samples. The comparisons below therefore use each system's *average*
concentration (non-detects as zero) to screen against MCLs and calculate
the Hazard Index, and report the *maximum* single result separately. Any
values exceeding a reference level are screening flags, not violations.
Update the table if EPA revises these values.

```{r}
#| label: ucmr5-reference-levels

ucmr5_reference <- tibble::tribble(
  ~contaminant_key, ~reference_ngL, ~reference_type,                ~hi_hbwc_ngL,
  "PFOA",            4.0,           "MCL (2024)",                   NA,
  "PFOS",            4.0,           "MCL (2024)",                   NA,
  "PFHXS",          10,             "MCL (2024)",                   10,
  "PFNA",           10,             "MCL (2024)",                   10,
  "HFPODA",         10,             "MCL (2024)",                   10,
  "PFBS",           NA,             "Hazard Index component only",  2000,
  "LITHIUM",     10000,             "Health reference level",       NA
)

missing_ref <- setdiff(ucmr5_reference$contaminant_key, unique(ucmr5_cook$contaminant_key))
if (length(missing_ref) > 0) {
  message("Reference contaminants not found in the Cook County results (check naming): ",
          paste(missing_ref, collapse = ", "))
}
```

## Summarize by system and contaminant

The next chunk summarizes results for each system and contaminant: the
number of samples and detections, the average concentration (non-detects
as zero), and the maximum detected concentration. It then attaches the
reference level and flags whether the average or maximum exceeds it.

```{r}
#| label: ucmr5-system-contaminant

ucmr5_cook_system_contaminant <- ucmr5_cook %>%
  group_by(PWSID, PWSName, Contaminant, contaminant_key, contaminant_group) %>%
  summarise(
    n_samples  = n(),
    n_detects  = sum(detected),
    mean_ngL   = mean(result_ngL_nd0, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_ngL    = if (any(detected)) max(result_ngL[detected], na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_,
    first_date = if (all(is.na(collection_date))) as.Date(NA) else min(collection_date, na.rm = TRUE),
    last_date  = if (all(is.na(collection_date))) as.Date(NA) else max(collection_date, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(ucmr5_reference, by = "contaminant_key") %>%
  mutate(
    mean_exceeds_reference = !is.na(reference_ngL) & mean_ngL > reference_ngL,
    max_exceeds_reference  = !is.na(reference_ngL) & !is.na(max_ngL) & max_ngL > reference_ngL
  )
```

## Summarize by system and join to service areas

Each system's results are then condensed into one row and joined by
`PWSID` to `cook_cws_with_violations`, adding the `ucmr5_*` fields:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `ucmr5_n_samples` | Total UCMR 5 results reported |
| `ucmr5_n_pfas_detected` | Number of distinct PFAS detected at or above the MRL |
| `ucmr5_any_pfas_detected` | Whether any PFAS was detected |
| `ucmr5_pfoa_mean_ngL`, `ucmr5_pfos_mean_ngL` | Average PFOA and PFOS (ng/L, non-detects as zero) |
| `ucmr5_pfas_max_ngL` | Highest single PFAS result (ng/L) |
| `ucmr5_hazard_index` | Hazard Index from average PFHxS, PFNA, HFPO-DA, and PFBS |
| `ucmr5_pfas_above_mcl` | Whether any PFAS with an MCL averages above it, or the Hazard Index exceeds 1 |
| `ucmr5_lithium_mean_ugL`, `ucmr5_lithium_max_ugL` | Average and highest lithium (µg/L) |
| `ucmr5_lithium_above_hrl` | Whether average lithium exceeds the 10 µg/L HRL |

Systems that did not report UCMR 5 results (mainly small systems not
selected for monitoring) receive `NA`.

```{r}
#| label: ucmr5-system-summary

key_mean <- function(df, key) {
  v <- df$mean_ngL[df$contaminant_key == key]
  if (length(v) == 0) NA_real_ else v[1]
}

ucmr5_system_summary <- ucmr5_cook_system_contaminant %>%
  group_by(PWSID) %>%
  group_modify(~ {
    pfas <- filter(.x, contaminant_group == "PFAS")
    li   <- filter(.x, contaminant_group == "Lithium")
    hi_parts <- filter(.x, !is.na(hi_hbwc_ngL))
    hazard_index <- if (nrow(hi_parts) > 0) sum(hi_parts$mean_ngL / hi_parts$hi_hbwc_ngL) else NA_real_
    tibble(
      ucmr5_n_samples         = sum(.x$n_samples),
      ucmr5_n_pfas_detected   = sum(pfas$n_detects > 0),
      ucmr5_any_pfas_detected = any(pfas$n_detects > 0),
      ucmr5_pfoa_mean_ngL     = key_mean(.x, "PFOA"),
      ucmr5_pfos_mean_ngL     = key_mean(.x, "PFOS"),
      ucmr5_pfas_max_ngL      = suppressWarnings(max(pfas$max_ngL, na.rm = TRUE)),
      ucmr5_hazard_index      = hazard_index,
      ucmr5_pfas_above_mcl    = any(pfas$mean_exceeds_reference) |
                                (!is.na(hazard_index) && hazard_index > 1),
      ucmr5_lithium_mean_ugL  = if (nrow(li) > 0) li$mean_ngL[1] / 1000 else NA_real_,
      ucmr5_lithium_max_ugL   = if (nrow(li) > 0) li$max_ngL[1] / 1000 else NA_real_,
      ucmr5_lithium_above_hrl = if (nrow(li) > 0) li$mean_exceeds_reference[1] else NA
    )
  }) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(ucmr5_pfas_max_ngL = if_else(is.finite(ucmr5_pfas_max_ngL), ucmr5_pfas_max_ngL, NA_real_))

cook_cws_with_violations <- cook_cws_with_violations %>%
  left_join(ucmr5_system_summary, by = "PWSID")

message(sum(!is.na(cook_cws_with_violations$ucmr5_n_samples)), " of ",
        nrow(cook_cws_with_violations), " service areas matched to UCMR 5 results.")
```

## Notes

- UCMR 5 results are a snapshot of 2023–2025 monitoring and are released
  in batches; systems whose results are not yet published appear as `NA`.
- Systems that buy water from another system (e.g., from Chicago) sample
  their own entry points, so purchased-water systems can show results that
  mostly reflect their supplier's source water.
- Exceeding a reference level in UCMR 5 monitoring is not a violation.
  UCMR results are not used for compliance, and PFAS MCL compliance
  monitoring does not begin until later in the decade.


# Export All Datasets {#sec-export}

Every Cook County dataset the pipeline produces is exported here in one
place, in two formats:

- **CSV**: one file per dataset in `data/csv/`. For spatial (`sf`)
  datasets, the CSV holds the attribute table plus `point_lon` and
  `point_lat`, a representative point inside each feature (WGS 84). The
  full geometry is in the GeoPackage.
- **GeoPackage**: a single file, `data/drinking_water_dataprep.gpkg`,
  with one layer per dataset. Spatial datasets are stored as feature
  layers and non-spatial datasets as plain attribute tables, so all
  of them open from one file in R (`sf::st_read()`), QGIS, or ArcGIS.

Each dataset is assigned to one of four tiers:

| Tier | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| **intermediate** | Cook County subsets and lookup tables used to build the later datasets, saved so each processing step can be traced and checked |
| **detailed** | Record-level data (one row per system, violation, sample, report, or result) |
| **analytical** | Analysis-ready datasets, including the service area polygons with all joined fields |
| **summary** | Aggregated tables (by system, contaminant, or reporting year) |

## Prepare intermediate subsets

Two of the statewide SDWA tables (geographic areas and service areas) are
used only to identify and describe Cook County systems. Their Cook County
rows are kept here as intermediate datasets. The `PWSID` list from
@sec-sdwis is also turned into a table that records how each system was
identified: through `COUNTY_SERVED`, through an intersecting service area
boundary, or both.

```{r}
#| label: export-intermediate-subsets

geo_areas_cook <- geo_areas %>% filter(PWSID %in% cook_pwsids)
svc_areas_cook <- svc_areas %>% filter(PWSID %in% cook_pwsids)

cook_pwsid_crosswalk <- tibble(PWSID = sort(union(cook_pwsids, cook_cws$PWSID))) %>%
  mutate(
    in_county_served  = PWSID %in% cook_pwsids,
    in_boundary_layer = PWSID %in% cook_cws$PWSID
  )
```

## Dataset registry

The registry below lists every exported dataset with its tier, the
pipeline section that creates it, and a short description. To export a
new dataset, add a row here. The same registry decides what goes into
the comprehensive `.RData` file (@sec-save-all).

```{r}
#| label: export-registry

dataset_registry <- tibble::tribble(
  ~name,                           ~tier,          ~section,     ~description,
  # Intermediate
  "cook_cws_raw",                  "intermediate", "boundaries", "Service area boundaries returned by the bounding-box query, before validity repair and clipping",
  "cook_pwsid_crosswalk",          "intermediate", "sdwis",      "Cook County PWSIDs and how each was identified (COUNTY_SERVED, boundary layer, or both)",
  "geo_areas_cook",                "intermediate", "sdwis",      "SDWA geographic area records for Cook County systems",
  "svc_areas_cook",                "intermediate", "sdwis",      "SDWA service area type records for Cook County systems",
  "ref_codes",                     "intermediate", "sdwis",      "SDWA reference code lookup table used to decode violation and contaminant codes",
  "lsl_cook_raw",                  "intermediate", "lsl",        "IEPA service line inventory reports for Cook County systems, as reported",
  "ucmr5_reference",               "intermediate", "ucmr5",      "Health-based reference levels used for UCMR 5 screening",
  # Detailed
  "pws_cook",                      "detailed",     "sdwis",      "Cook County public water system inventory (all SDWA fields)",
  "violations_cook",               "detailed",     "sdwis",      "Decoded SDWA violations and enforcement records for Cook County systems",
  "lcr_cook",                      "detailed",     "sdwis",      "Lead and Copper Rule sample results for Cook County systems",
  "cook_lsl_history",              "detailed",     "lsl",        "Standardized service line material inventories, all reporting years",
  "ucmr5_cook",                    "detailed",     "ucmr5",      "Standardized UCMR 5 results (PFAS and lithium) for Cook County systems",
  # Analytical
  "cook_county",                   "analytical",   "boundaries", "Cook County boundary polygon",
  "cook_cws",                      "analytical",   "boundaries", "Community water system service areas clipped to Cook County",
  "cook_cws_with_violations",      "analytical",   "ucmr5",      "Service areas joined to violation, lead service line (lsl_*), and UCMR 5 (ucmr5_*) fields",
  "pws_cook_summary",              "analytical",   "sdwis",      "System attributes joined to violation counts",
  "cook_lsl_latest",               "analytical",   "lsl",        "Each system's most recent service line inventory",
  # Summary
  "violation_summary",             "summary",      "sdwis",      "Violation counts and most recent violation date by system",
  "lsl_summary_by_year",           "summary",      "lsl",        "Service line material totals across Cook County systems by reporting year",
  "ucmr5_cook_system_contaminant", "summary",      "ucmr5",      "UCMR 5 results by system and contaminant, with reference-level flags",
  "ucmr5_system_summary",          "summary",      "ucmr5",      "One-row-per-system UCMR 5 summary"
)
```

## Export helpers

Three helpers do the export:

- `gpkg_safe_names()` makes column names unique without regard to case,
  because GeoPackage (SQLite) treats names such as `PWS_Name` and
  `PWS_NAME` as the same column. The known case is already handled in
  @sec-sdwis; this is a safeguard for any new fields. A later duplicate
  gets a numeric suffix (e.g. `NAME_1`). Only the exported copies are
  renamed; the R objects are unchanged.
- `csv_table()` returns the table to write to CSV: the data itself, or for
  `sf` objects the attributes plus a representative point (`point_lon`,
  `point_lat`). `st_point_on_surface()` is used instead of the centroid so
  that the point always falls inside the polygon.
- `export_dataset()` writes one dataset to CSV and to the GeoPackage
  (replacing any earlier layer of the same name) and returns one row of
  metadata for the manifest.

```{r}
#| label: export-helpers

gpkg_safe_names <- function(nm) {
  key <- make.unique(tolower(nm), sep = "_")
  renamed <- key != tolower(nm)
  nm[renamed] <- paste0(nm[renamed], substring(key[renamed], nchar(nm[renamed]) + 1))
  nm
}

csv_table <- function(x) {
  if (!inherits(x, "sf")) return(x)
  pts <- suppressWarnings(st_point_on_surface(st_geometry(st_transform(x, 4326))))
  xy  <- t(vapply(seq_along(pts), function(i) {
    if (st_is_empty(pts[[i]])) c(NA_real_, NA_real_) else st_coordinates(pts[[i]])[1, 1:2]
  }, numeric(2)))
  st_drop_geometry(x) %>%
    mutate(point_lon = xy[, 1], point_lat = xy[, 2])
}

export_dataset <- function(x, name, tier) {
  x <- if (inherits(x, "sf")) x else as.data.frame(x)

  attr_cols <- setdiff(names(x), if (inherits(x, "sf")) attr(x, "sf_column"))
  names(x)[match(attr_cols, names(x))] <- gpkg_safe_names(attr_cols)

  csv_path <- file.path(out_csv_dir, paste0(name, ".csv"))
  csv_out  <- csv_table(x)
  write_csv(csv_out, csv_path, na = "")

  st_write(x, out_gpkg_path, layer = name, delete_layer = TRUE, quiet = TRUE)

  tibble(
    name          = name,
    tier          = tier,
    n_rows        = nrow(x),
    n_columns     = ncol(csv_out),
    geometry_type = if (inherits(x, "sf")) paste(unique(as.character(st_geometry_type(x))), collapse = "/") else "none",
    crs           = if (inherits(x, "sf")) st_crs(x)$input else NA_character_,
    csv_file      = csv_path,
    gpkg_layer    = name
  )
}
```

## Write datasets

The chunk below exports every registry dataset that exists in this run.
Any dataset that was not created (for example, because a section was
skipped) is reported and left out rather than stopping the export. The
GeoPackage is rebuilt from scratch each run so that it never holds stale
layers from an earlier run.

```{r}
#| label: export-datasets

pipeline_env <- environment()

dataset_available <- vapply(dataset_registry$name, exists, logical(1),
                            envir = pipeline_env, inherits = FALSE)
if (any(!dataset_available)) {
  message("Not exported (object not created in this run): ",
          paste(dataset_registry$name[!dataset_available], collapse = ", "))
}
datasets_to_export <- dataset_registry[dataset_available, ]

if (file.exists(out_gpkg_path)) file.remove(out_gpkg_path)

export_log <- purrr::pmap_dfr(
  list(datasets_to_export$name, datasets_to_export$tier),
  function(name, tier) {
    message("Exporting ", name, " (", tier, ")")
    export_dataset(get(name, envir = pipeline_env), name, tier)
  }
)
```

## Manifest and data dictionary

Two documentation tables are written alongside the datasets, both as CSV
and as GeoPackage layers:

- **`dataset_manifest`**: one row per exported dataset, with its tier,
  source section, description, size, geometry type, and file locations.
- **`data_dictionary`**: one row per column of every exported dataset,
  with its R class and the share of missing values.

```{r}
#| label: export-manifest-dictionary

dataset_manifest <- datasets_to_export %>%
  left_join(export_log, by = c("name", "tier")) %>%
  mutate(exported = format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %Z"))

data_dictionary <- purrr::map_dfr(datasets_to_export$name, function(name) {
  x <- get(name, envir = pipeline_env)
  if (inherits(x, "sf")) x <- st_drop_geometry(x)
  tibble(
    dataset     = name,
    column      = names(x),
    r_class     = vapply(x, function(col) paste(class(col), collapse = "/"), character(1)),
    pct_missing = vapply(x, function(col) round(100 * mean(is.na(col)), 1), numeric(1))
  )
}) %>%
  left_join(select(dataset_registry, dataset = name, tier), by = "dataset") %>%
  relocate(tier, .after = dataset)

write_csv(dataset_manifest, file.path(out_csv_dir, "dataset_manifest.csv"), na = "")
write_csv(data_dictionary,  file.path(out_csv_dir, "data_dictionary.csv"),  na = "")
st_write(as.data.frame(dataset_manifest), out_gpkg_path, layer = "dataset_manifest",
         delete_layer = TRUE, quiet = TRUE)
st_write(as.data.frame(data_dictionary),  out_gpkg_path, layer = "data_dictionary",
         delete_layer = TRUE, quiet = TRUE)

print(count(dataset_manifest, tier, name = "n_datasets"))
message("Exported ", nrow(dataset_manifest), " datasets to ", out_csv_dir, "/ and ",
        out_gpkg_path, " (", round(file.size(out_gpkg_path) / 1024^2, 1), " MB)")
```

# Save R Data Files {#sec-save}

Two `.RData` files are written: a lightweight one with the objects the
rendered brief needs, and a comprehensive one holding every exported
dataset. Both keep `sf` objects as native R objects for convenience. The
brief itself imports its spatial data from the GeoPackage
(`data/drinking_water_dataprep.gpkg`), which is the main format for all
spatial outputs.

## Essential objects for rendering

Only the objects referenced by `drinking_water.qmd`'s evaluated
(`eval: true`) chunks are persisted, so the `.RData` file stays small and
the rendered brief depends only on what it needs:

| Object | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `cook_county` | `sf` polygon of the Cook County boundary, used as the reference outline on the brief's interactive leaflet map. |
| `cook_cws_with_violations` | `sf` polygons of community water system service areas joined to the system-level SDWA violation summary, each system's most recent IEPA lead service line inventory (`lsl_*` fields), and its UCMR 5 summary (`ucmr5_*` fields). This is the main data source for the brief's Analysis section, including the interactive map (fill, hover labels, and the derived violation-density measure computed in the brief). |
| `ucmr5_cook_system_contaminant` | UCMR 5 results summarized by system and contaminant, used for the brief's contaminant-level UCMR 5 summary table. |

The chunk below saves these objects with `xz` compression.

```{r}
#| label: save-rdata

save(cook_county, cook_cws_with_violations, ucmr5_cook_system_contaminant,
     file = out_rdata_path, compress = "xz")

message("Saved essential rendering data (cook_county, cook_cws_with_violations, ",
        "ucmr5_cook_system_contaminant) to ", out_rdata_path)
```

## Comprehensive data file {#sec-save-all}

`data/drinking_water_dataprep_all.RData` holds every dataset in the
registry (@sec-export), across all four tiers, as native R objects: `sf`
objects keep their geometry, and dates, factors, and logical columns keep
their types. It also holds:

- `dataset_registry`, `dataset_manifest`, and `data_dictionary`, which
  describe the datasets.
- `dataprep_info`, a list recording when the file was created, the source
  files used, and the R and package versions.

Loading this one file restores the full set of analysis data without
re-running the pipeline or reading the CSV and GeoPackage outputs:

```r
load("data/drinking_water_dataprep_all.RData")
dataset_manifest   # what is available, by tier
```

Large statewide and national source tables (`pws`, `violations`,
`geo_areas`, `svc_areas`, `lcr_samples`, `lsl_raw`, `ucmr5_raw`) are left
out because they can be re-read from the downloaded source files.

```{r}
#| label: save-rdata-all

dataprep_info <- list(
  created       = Sys.time(),
  objects       = datasets_to_export$name,
  missing       = dataset_registry$name[!dataset_available],
  sdwa_source   = zip_path,
  lsl_source    = if (exists("lsl_inventory_path")) lsl_inventory_path else NA_character_,
  ucmr5_source  = if (exists("ucmr5_zip_path")) ucmr5_zip_path else NA_character_,
  csv_dir       = out_csv_dir,
  gpkg_path     = out_gpkg_path,
  r_version     = R.version.string,
  packages      = vapply(c("dplyr", "tidyr", "readr", "sf", "httr2", "tigris"),
                         function(p) as.character(packageVersion(p)), character(1))
)

save(list = c(datasets_to_export$name, "dataset_registry", "dataset_manifest",
              "data_dictionary", "dataprep_info"),
     file = out_rdata_all_path, envir = pipeline_env, compress = "xz")

message("Saved ", nrow(datasets_to_export), " datasets plus manifest, dictionary, and ",
        "run information to ", out_rdata_all_path,
        " (", round(file.size(out_rdata_all_path) / 1024^2, 1), " MB)")
```
